chasing_ghosts.description: Improved instruction-goal localization does not translate into competitive complete navigation.
chasing_ghosts.conditions: R2R with RGB-D panoramas, supplied poses and discrete reachable graph nodes.
chasing_ghosts.cause: The ghost endpoint belief is consumed by a separate local graph-node controller; localization quality alone does not solve route selection and stopping.
chasing_ghosts.evidence: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Tables 1–2, PDF pp.7–8: localization 44.9% versus 32.2%, but unseen navigation SR/SPL 35/31. DEDUCTION: interface bottleneck rather than measured causal attribution.
chasing_ghosts.followups: DUET/topological planners change control and representation; HNR/SALI add predicted content. No matched belief-versus-controller intervention was reviewed.

chasing_ghosts.description: Normalized ghost beliefs have no demonstrated calibration under pose error or ambiguous instructions.
chasing_ghosts.conditions: Variable-length instructions, incorrect pose/depth or multiple plausible instruction routes.
chasing_ghosts.cause: Learned motion/observation likelihoods, a fixed six-step ghost rollout, and normalized products do not establish valid likelihood independence or coverage.
chasing_ghosts.evidence: DEDUCTION: Sections 3–4, PDF pp.3–6; tracker/modules/navigators.py:142–189,279–286 and tracker/modules/loss.py:20–36 at the dossier commit.
chasing_ghosts.followups: Later map-based and imagined-view papers in this assignment do not report matched posterior-coverage tests.

cotvla.description: Generated visual subgoals can fail to specify a useful reachable action target.
cotvla.conditions: Novel manipulation tasks requiring visual subgoals outside fine-tuning support.
cotvla.cause: Language/image-conditioned generation does not explicitly enforce the action-conditioned reachability of the target.
cotvla.evidence: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 3, PDF p.8, five trials on each of two novel tasks: generated goals 20%/0% versus demonstration goals 60%/40%. Small sample and privileged targets limit attribution.
cotvla.followups: FantasyVLN and WorldVLN use different navigation tasks; neither supplies a matched manipulation reachability test.

cotvla.description: Visual-token generation slows decisions and action chunks postpone observation feedback.
cotvla.conditions: Ten-action execution chunks, especially when the environment changes within a chunk.
cotvla.cause: Autoregressive generation of 256 visual tokens precedes action prediction; the policy obtains a new real image at chunk boundaries.
cotvla.evidence: AUTHOR ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: Section 5, PDF p.8, approximately sevenfold slowdown at chunk length ten and missing high-frequency feedback.
cotvla.followups: FantasyVLN removes explicit visual CoT at deployment and reports faster actions (Table 2); this shifts burden into training and does not verify within-chunk control in the same task.
cotvla.status: Shifted into another cost or limitation

cvaml.description: Finite-sample variance correction can retain bias and raise sampling costs.
cvaml.conditions: Stochastic transitions with a finite number of next-state samples.
cvaml.cause: The inspected estimator uses population variance divided by N; with iid samples and fixed value, that differs from unbiased sample variance divided by N. Sample-dependent action selection adds further dependencies.
cvaml.evidence: INSPECTED CODE: CVAML loss discussion and immutable links in 02_repository_audit.md. EXECUTED TEST: evidence/02/logic_check_results.json enumerates 16 N=4 ±1 samples; corrected mean loss 0.0625 versus approximately zero with unbiased variance. This is a restricted arithmetic counterexample, not a benchmark result.
cvaml.followups: No inspected follow-up supplies a correction for this exact estimator and dependency structure.
cvaml.status: Still unresolved in the reviewed literature
cvaml.confidence: High for the stated iid fixed-value counterexample; uncertain for benchmark impact

cvaml.description: Value equivalence for one value function does not preserve all future instruction-dependent distinctions.
cvaml.conditions: Changing language goals or rewards after learning a task-specific latent model.
cvaml.cause: The objective preserves expected values for its selected value function, allowing state distinctions irrelevant to that function to disappear.
cvaml.evidence: DEDUCTION: main objective and Appendix proof, PDF pp.18–20; the existence argument assumes a compact connected setting and a suitable value mapping. Appendix C.4 p.23 shows auxiliary BYOL loss remains important.
cvaml.followups: NavQ predicts goal-dependent semantic successors; WoMAP learns detector-derived rewards. Neither establishes universal goal-change preservation or action-risk calibration.

dinowm.description: Image-goal feature planning does not itself provide language-goal reward semantics.
dinowm.conditions: Tasks specified by text rather than an available target image.
dinowm.cause: The planner optimizes distance to a specified visual target in frozen DINO feature space.
dinowm.evidence: AUTHOR METHOD: Section 3 and task evaluation, PDF pp.3–6; Table 2 shows patch features help PushT but does not validate language understanding.
dinowm.followups: WoMAP adds VLM proposals and language-conditioned distilled object rewards, with physical object-reaching tests. This adds detector and VLM errors and is not broad instruction-following validation.

dinowm.description: Feature similarity can reward predicted outcomes that are not achievable or task-correct.
dinowm.conditions: Out-of-support actions, aliased views or multimodal futures during CEM search.
dinowm.cause: A deterministic feature predictor and feature-distance goal objective need not preserve all physical constraints; optimizing them can select model errors.
dinowm.evidence: DEDUCTION from Section 3 and inspected planner; Table 1 task successes do not test calibrated confidence or adversarial model exploitation.
dinowm.followups: WoMAP extends the reward interface but retains optimizer/model/reward error; no matched intervention establishes resolution.

dreamer.description: Avoiding online candidate search requires learning an actor and value model on imagined trajectories.
dreamer.conditions: Tasks where latency at action selection matters but training compute is available.
dreamer.cause: Dreamer amortizes PlaNet-style latent planning through actor/value optimization rather than solving the search anew at deployment.
dreamer.evidence: AUTHOR METHOD and PAPER EXPERIMENT: Sections 3–4 and Figure 6, PDF pp.3–6; mean score 823 after 5M steps on 20 DMC tasks. This does not establish equal compute.
dreamer.followups: Dreamer addresses PlaNet online search cost; later Dreamer versions extend scaling. The cost moves into behavior learning and value approximation.
dreamer.status: Shifted into another cost or limitation

dreamer.description: Imagined actor improvement can exploit model or value errors outside collected support.
dreamer.conditions: Long imagined trajectories or policy updates into poorly observed regions.
dreamer.cause: Policy gradients optimize returns supplied by learned dynamics and bootstrapped values; neither provides a general off-distribution correctness guarantee.
dreamer.evidence: DEDUCTION: Dreamer latent rollout/value objectives; World Models provides a direct exploitation example, while Dreamer benchmark gains do not isolate this failure mode.
dreamer.followups: Iterative data collection and later Dreamer models mitigate distribution mismatch, but no reviewed evidence resolves all out-of-support goal-conditioned navigation errors.
dreamer.status: Still unresolved in the reviewed literature

dreamwalker.description: Distance prediction remains a stronger bottleneck than future image fidelity in the paper intervention.
dreamwalker.conditions: Unseen continuous VLN episodes requiring branch ranking.
dreamwalker.cause: The distance evaluator scores imagined states; a visually reasonable branch can still receive the wrong task-progress score.
dreamwalker.evidence: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 2 p.7 gives SR 49 normally versus 54 with oracle views; Figure 4 reaches 100% with full privileged distance replacement. Oracle interventions are not deployable methods.
dreamwalker.followups: HNR improves fixed-policy future features; NavQ adds semantic/distance supervision. Neither supplies a matched resolution of DREAMWALKER distance calibration.

dreamwalker.description: The printed distance/reward signs cannot be resolved against released model code.
dreamwalker.conditions: Attempting a faithful reimplementation of Eqs.11–12.
dreamwalker.cause: The text describes progress toward a goal, while printed reward/softmax signs appear to favor larger distance; retrieved official repository contains documentation rather than model source.
dreamwalker.evidence: UNVERIFIED: Eqs.11–12 versus prose, PDF method section; official repository README at ab7c9a5c9d07742e30e4cf99132cf1f61bb83de5.
dreamwalker.followups: No inspected correction or executable official implementation resolves the sign ambiguity.
dreamwalker.confidence: High for the documentation gap; unknown for intended implementation

eoe.description: Image semantic novelty scores are not established estimates of unsafe or instruction-inconsistent navigation actions.
eoe.conditions: Familiar objects with unsafe transitions, or unknown categories absent from generated negative labels.
eoe.cause: The score compares CLIP similarity to generated class descriptions, without a transition/action outcome variable or exhaustive unknown-class coverage.
eoe.evidence: PAPER EXPERIMENT: pp.6–8 fine-grained FPR95/AUROC 60.52/81.82, far-ImageNet 30.09/92.96; INSPECTED CODE: cosine overlap filter at 0.85 for ImageNet20. DEDUCTION: semantic novelty differs from navigation risk.
eoe.followups: No matched navigation-risk follow-up was reviewed; EOE must remain adjacent OOD prior art.

fantasyvln.description: Full multi-part navigation success remains very low despite relative gains.
fantasyvln.conditions: The evaluated long complete-task benchmark rather than isolated subgoal success.
fantasyvln.cause: A long sequence of grounding/action decisions can fail even when per-subtask completion improves; the experiment does not isolate the causal distribution of these failures.
fantasyvln.evidence: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 1 p.6, SR 2.44, ISR 11.01, CSR 9.64; more than 97% of complete tasks fail. No independently reproduced decomposition.
fantasyvln.followups: MonoDream/NavForesee/WorldVLN evaluate different task/sensing settings, so their headline successes do not establish a solution on this protocol.
fantasyvln.status: Still unresolved in the reviewed literature

fantasyvln.description: Action-token alignment does not establish that visual reasoning is faithful or necessary at inference.
fantasyvln.conditions: Attributing improvements to actual reasoning rather than auxiliary representation learning.
fantasyvln.cause: Training aligns branches, while direct deployment can act without explicit visual CoT; multiple training changes share credit.
fantasyvln.evidence: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 3, visual-only non-CoT ISR 11.19 versus full 11.01; alignment removal SR 0. INSPECTED CODE: trainer ranges cited in dossier confirm non-CoT teacher to CoT action alignment.
fantasyvln.followups: MonoDream and VLN-SIG also use auxiliary prediction. No matched counterfactual intervention establishes faithful reasoning across these systems.

genex.description: Long self-consistent generated trajectories need not describe the actual occluded environment.
genex.conditions: Using simulated views to answer questions about hidden physical facts or update navigation confidence.
genex.cause: Conditional on a fixed real observation history and fixed model, additional generated samples are computed from that information; loop closure can be satisfied by a consistently false world.
genex.evidence: DEDUCTION: generative pipeline; PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 2 p.9 IELC 0.105 streets/0.092 indoors and synthetic GenEx-EQA do not measure truth of hidden real environments.
genex.followups: SALI persists imagined nodes; WorldVLN assimilates later real observations. Real observations add evidence, but no reviewed study establishes reliable confidence for hidden facts from generation alone.
genex.status: Still unresolved in the reviewed literature
genex.confidence: High for information distinction; medium for system-level practical impact

hnr.description: Semantic feature prediction degrades with distance and occlusion.
hnr.conditions: Longer lookahead branches entering unobserved regions in R2R-CE/RxR-CE.
hnr.cause: Rendered features must extrapolate geometry/semantics not directly contained in the observed feature field.
hnr.evidence: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Figure 5 p.7 shows declining similarity with distance; Table 3 predicted SR 60.74 versus oracle 63.13 under fixed lookahead policy; Table 6 soft targets outperform hard targets.
hnr.followups: NavMorph adds contextual adaptation and improves HNR; SC²-WM adds calibration and delayed real-observation adaptation. Gains do not eliminate the equal-sensing occluded-region oracle gap.

hnr.description: Maximizing descendant scores can favor an overoptimistic noisy branch.
hnr.conditions: More candidate descendants or correlated errors in unseen-branch evaluation.
hnr.cause: Eq.15 takes a maximum without a demonstrated uncertainty correction or calibrated confidence bound.
hnr.evidence: DEDUCTION: Eq.15, method section; no risk-calibration or search-width bias experiment was identified in reviewed tables.
hnr.followups: NavQ avoids explicit rollout through successor semantics; SC²-WM adapts features. Neither directly tests or removes the maximum-selection bias in the same planner.

imaginenav.description: Local mapless imagination can revisit regions and spend path length on unproductive choices.
imaginenav.conditions: Long object-goal searches with repeated visually similar regions.
imaginenav.cause: Limited persistent spatial memory and proposal constraints restrict global exploration history.
imaginenav.evidence: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 1 p.7 HM3D SR/SPL 53/23.8 versus VLFM 52.5/30.4. DEDUCTION: lower efficiency is compatible with, but does not prove, revisitation as its cause.
imaginenav.followups: ImagineNav++ arXiv:2512.17435 adds memory/selective foveation. Its project and forthcoming-code status were inspected, but a matched full implementation/experimental audit is outside this dossier.

imaginenav.description: Novel-view prediction errors leave a substantial action-selection gap.
imaginenav.conditions: Unseen scenes and viewpoints outside the synthesizer training distribution.
imaginenav.cause: The action selector depends on generated candidate views whose appearance/content can be wrong.
imaginenav.evidence: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 1 p.7 oracle views raise SR from 53 to 62 on HM3D and from 51 to 59 on HSSD.
imaginenav.followups: HNR changes representation and WMNav changes the scoring interface; cross-protocol gains do not resolve the matched ImagineNav oracle gap.
imaginenav.status: Still unresolved in the reviewed literature

lcvn.description: Offline endpoint success does not establish collision-free closed-loop instruction following.
lcvn.conditions: Open-loop predicted trajectories, particularly novel scenes with alternate valid routes.
lcvn.cause: The evaluated endpoint threshold and expert-latent reward omit intervening collision and real-observation correction evidence.
lcvn.evidence: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Tables 1–2 pp.8–9: unified unseen SR 0.27 versus separate 0.19, despite separate model better SSIM/LPIPS; success is endpoint distance below average step size. INSPECTED CODE: actor uses detached returns and REINFORCE rather than a gradient through frozen DFOT.
lcvn.followups: WorldVLN uses segmented real observations, while WorldMAP/PiJEPA remain current leads. No matched physical closed-loop validation was reviewed.

learning_to_map.description: Ensemble variance and repeated map fusion do not provide validated calibrated exploration uncertainty.
learning_to_map.conditions: Shared model bias or repeated correlated observations in active object-goal navigation.
learning_to_map.cause: Ensemble members can agree incorrectly, and registered repeated predictions are not independent evidence; UCB score construction lacks demonstrated coverage.
learning_to_map.evidence: DEDUCTION: ensemble prediction and UCB mechanism; PAPER EXPERIMENT: Tables 1–2 p.7 show SR/SPL 34.3/13.3 and IoU 25.6, not calibration guarantees.
learning_to_map.followups: SGM uses masked map completion and WMNav heuristic VLM curiosity; neither resolves posterior coverage or shared-bias detection in this protocol.

learning_to_map.description: Active semantic mapping requires privileged training maps, accurate pose and multiple predictor evaluations.
learning_to_map.conditions: Deployment without reliable pose or training scenes with annotated semantic occupancy.
learning_to_map.cause: Map registration relies on known pose; supervised targets and four-model ensembles introduce annotation and inference costs.
learning_to_map.evidence: AUTHOR METHOD: map construction/training and ensemble details in dossier; no pose-error ablation establishes robustness.
learning_to_map.followups: SGM introduces masked-map pretraining and priors, partially changing supervision, but retains semantic-map/perception dependencies.

lookbeforeleap.description: Teacher-heavy model data and frozen deterministic short-horizon prediction poorly cover policy errors.
lookbeforeleap.conditions: Actions and scenes outside the environment-model training distribution.
lookbeforeleap.cause: The predictor is trained before policy use and is not corrected online; deterministic features compress multiple possible outcomes.
lookbeforeleap.evidence: AUTHOR METHOD and DEDUCTION: two-stage training/rollout sections; Table 1 p.12 unseen SR 24.6 versus model-free 21.5 establishes early utility but not shift robustness.
lookbeforeleap.followups: DREAMWALKER/HNR strengthen predictions; NavMorph and SC²-WM add adaptation. SC²-WM specifically supplies delayed real-observation residual updates, but on a different architecture and CE protocol.

monodream.description: Longer future prediction supervision can hurt under partial observability.
monodream.conditions: Monocular VLN with prediction targets beyond immediately visible geometry.
monodream.cause: Targets become less identifiable from the current/history view, and auxiliary prediction can emphasize unreliable future details.
monodream.evidence: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 6 p.7 SR 39.1/34.3/29.2 for horizons one/two/three; Table 5 current-depth-only 42.2 versus future-depth-only 39.8. DEDUCTION: target ambiguity is plausible, not experimentally isolated.
monodream.followups: FantasyVLN also uses training-time imagination; NavForesee keeps future structures in action computation. No matched equal-data horizon intervention demonstrates a resolution.
monodream.status: Still unresolved in the reviewed literature

monodream.description: The inspected official release does not provide the full auxiliary training pipeline needed to reproduce all four prediction objectives.
monodream.conditions: Reproducing training ablations rather than loading published navigation weights.
monodream.cause: The released RoboOrchardLab project exposes model, processor, inference and evaluation, but the inspected project listing lacks the complete paper-specific auxiliary trainer.
monodream.evidence: INSPECTED CODE: HorizonRobotics/RoboOrchardLab commit 48ac43987df9ac1ba40fef72dd7a2b4679c592b4; projects/monodream and models/monodream files listed in the dossier.
monodream.followups: Official implementation release resolves the earlier no-code search result for inference; a faithful full training reproduction remains unverified.
monodream.confidence: High for inspected release scope; no claim about inaccessible future/private code

navforesee.description: Predicted target structures are not established as faithful consequences of alternative candidate actions.
navforesee.conditions: Using semantic/depth futures for branch choice under ambiguous or unusual layouts.
navforesee.cause: Task-conditioned future supervision may encode desired goal templates; it does not alone identify action-specific environment transitions.
navforesee.evidence: DEDUCTION: future prediction/action pipeline; PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 2 p.7 full SR 66.2 versus 58.6 without long-horizon prediction shows utility, not physical counterfactual fidelity.
navforesee.followups: WorldVLN and LCVN use other action/observation interfaces; SC²-WM adds observed residual adaptation. None is a matched counterfactual-validity test of NavForesee.

navmorph.description: Online context adaptation improves scores but does not establish reliable correction of confidently wrong predictions.
navmorph.conditions: Unseen CE scenes and biased stored context.
navmorph.cause: Contextual memory supplies retrieved features without a calibrated confidence gate; latent alignment can preserve shared prediction bias.
navmorph.evidence: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 3 p.8 SR 47.91 versus 45.08 without self-evolution; DEDUCTION: Eq.2–3 memory weights are not correctness probabilities.
navmorph.followups: SC²-WM adds learned feature/state refinement and delayed real-observation TTA, with further CE gains. Residual-to-correct-action reliability is still not isolated.

navmorph.description: Cross-episode memory makes evaluation depend on reset, ordering and prior test-scene exposure.
navmorph.conditions: Transductive test evaluation across multiple episodes in a scene.
navmorph.cause: Memory slots retain scene/context information, and replacement behavior changes available knowledge.
navmorph.evidence: AUTHOR ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: PDF p.8 discussion of test-scene memory/fairness; Figure 4 memory size 1000 performs best and smaller/larger settings can hurt.
navmorph.followups: SC²-WM also adapts online, making episode-reset and matched exposure controls necessary. No reviewed ordering/reset factorial resolves comparability.
navmorph.status: Still unresolved in the reviewed literature

navq.description: Successor semantic averaging can erase rare or route-specific evidence.
navq.conditions: Long discounted continuations, multiple equal shortest routes, or route-faithful instructions.
navq.cause: A fixed-dimensional weighted semantic target summarizes future captions under a selected continuation rather than representing all branch-specific consequences.
navq.evidence: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 4 p.8 gamma 0/.3/.5/.7 SR 51.12/51.95/53.22/50.89; Table 3 p.7 predicted full SR 53.22 versus oracle 59.27. INSPECTED CODE: dataset uses one stored shortest path per target.
navq.followups: UNeMo adds task-conditioned future features and SC²-WM works in CE, but neither supplies a matched remedy for aggregated-semantic ambiguity.
navq.status: Still unresolved in the reviewed literature

navq.description: Shortest continuation is not mathematically unique without a tie-breaking or graph assumption.
navq.conditions: Graphs containing equal-length shortest paths to the same destination.
navq.cause: Distinct first actions can share a shortest destination path length; the implementation chooses one stored path operationally.
navq.evidence: DEDUCTION/EXECUTED TEST: diamond-graph counterexample in evidence/02/logic_check_results.json; source dataset target construction, lines 180–244 at the dossier commit.
navq.followups: The released target construction resolves operational labeling via a stored path, but does not establish the printed general uniqueness claim.
navq.status: Still unresolved in the reviewed literature
navq.confidence: High: the unqualified uniqueness claim has a counterexample; stored-path labeling remains well defined

nwm.description: Diffusion-based trajectory evaluation and restricted CEM candidates impose compute and expressivity costs.
nwm.conditions: Online action planning over multiple imagined time steps.
nwm.cause: Each candidate requires generated predictions; the released planner repeats one displacement across the horizon with a final yaw adjustment instead of optimizing fully independent per-step actions.
nwm.evidence: INSPECTED CODE: planner.py:217–299 at the dossier commit; PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 2 p.7 is offline ATE/RPE, not closed-loop SR.
nwm.followups: LCVN trains an actor and unifies language/video/action generation, moving cost into training and changing the evaluation. No matched cost/expressivity resolution was reviewed.
nwm.status: Shifted into another cost or limitation

nwm.description: Offline video/trajectory errors do not establish safe causal action predictions in deployment.
nwm.conditions: Actions outside logged support, moving obstacles or long physical navigation.
nwm.cause: Observational action-conditioned training plus endpoint error metrics does not identify unsupported interventions or validate all intermediate transitions.
nwm.evidence: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Tables 1–2 pp.6–7 report LPIPS and ATE/RPE; no physical safety claim follows. Access limit: high-resolution SACSoN/HuRoN data are not redistributable in official README.
nwm.followups: Vid2World improves causal masking/guidance; LCVN adds language. Different datasets and offline metrics do not resolve this validity gap.

pathdreamer.description: Image-generation gains were evaluated with a privileged future navigation graph.
pathdreamer.conditions: Interpreting navigation results as planning through completely unknown geometry.
pathdreamer.cause: The navigation evaluation supplies future graph connectivity while replacing only future visual observations.
pathdreamer.evidence: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 3 p.8 horizon-three SR 50.4 versus repetition 40.6 and oracle 59.3; evaluation explicitly uses ground-truth future graph.
pathdreamer.followups: DREAMWALKER predicts waypoints and HNR evaluates continuous candidates, partly reducing the oracle-graph assumption while introducing waypoint/geometry prediction error.

pathdreamer.description: Generated structure degrades over successive unseen views.
pathdreamer.conditions: One to six synthesized steps into occluded geometry.
pathdreamer.cause: Autoregressive structure hallucinations accumulate; training RGB generation with ground-truth structure adds stage mismatch.
pathdreamer.evidence: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 1 p.7 unseen semantic mIoU 78.3 one-step versus 50.8 across one to six steps.
pathdreamer.followups: HNR reduces pixel-generation cost and SALI preserves imagined nodes; neither validates the truth of long-horizon occluded structure under equal sensing.

planet.description: Receding-horizon latent CEM requires repeated candidate rollouts at each action decision.
planet.conditions: Latency-limited control with long horizons or many candidate sequences.
planet.cause: Compute grows with candidate count, horizon and optimizer iterations; one sampled stochastic rollout per candidate can also produce noisy ranking.
planet.evidence: AUTHOR METHOD: latent CEM procedure and inspected planner source; Figures 4–5 test performance, not a universal latency bound.
planet.followups: Dreamer amortizes search into a learned actor/value model. Online cost is reduced by accepting training cost and approximation error.
planet.status: Shifted into another cost or limitation

planet.description: Selecting high predicted reward can exploit transition and reward-model errors.
planet.conditions: Long rollouts or actions poorly supported by real experience.
planet.cause: The same learned model both predicts outcomes and supplies the objective optimized by search.
planet.evidence: DEDUCTION: RSSM/reward planning pipeline; World Models supplies direct virtual-versus-real exploitation evidence, while PlaNet tests do not establish general calibration.
planet.followups: Dreamer changes policy optimization and CVAML corrects a different value-aware estimator bias; neither is proof of physically correct unsupported rollouts.
planet.status: Still unresolved in the reviewed literature

sali.description: Persistent imagined nodes can retain incorrect room/object structure as planning evidence.
sali.conditions: Atypical layouts or errors in generated unseen views.
sali.cause: Heuristic pruning and score fusion do not provide calibrated provenance weights separating observed from synthesized content.
sali.evidence: DEDUCTION: imagined graph/memory method; qualitative imagery and PSNR are not hidden-world truth tests.
sali.followups: HNR/NavMorph/SC²-WM alter representations and adaptation; GenEx improves consistency. None directly demonstrates correct recovery from false persistent SALI memory.
sali.status: Still unresolved in the reviewed literature

sali.description: Headline and ablation performance cannot be fully reconciled from the inspected material.
sali.conditions: Attributing the large reported gain to imagination rather than a configuration or baseline difference.
sali.cause: Main R2R SPL 78 differs from full-system ablation SPL 70/71, and no verified official code resolves the configuration mapping.
sali.evidence: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 1 p.6 versus Table 2 p.7; source/access record in dossier. These numbers are author-reported and unexecuted.
sali.followups: No reviewed follow-up supplies a matched independent reproduction or configuration reconciliation.

sc2wm.description: The broad ambiguity about whether correction uses any real next observation is resolved by the released asynchronous TTA branch.
sc2wm.conditions: Interpreting immediate endogenous latent delta versus delayed deployment adaptation.
sc2wm.cause: Main-paper notation mixes current/next targets; immediate state refinement and delayed TTA use different signals.
sc2wm.evidence: INSPECTED CODE: ss_trainer_ETP.py:2246–2308 compares prior predicted candidate features with the next real panorama using cosine residual; supplement PDF pp.15–16 describes FRL and Table 6. Immediate Eq.9 delta remains predicted next latent minus current latent.
sc2wm.followups: The paper supplement and official release resolve existence/timing for this inspected branch. This does not certify correctness of all formulas or confidence calibration.
sc2wm.status: Resolved within a clearly specified setting

sc2wm.description: Residual-triggered adaptation is not yet established to improve decisions under confidently wrong dynamics or residual misalignment.
sc2wm.conditions: Domain shifts, ambiguous action selection, prediction/observation mismatch, or entropy confidently favoring a wrong action.
sc2wm.cause: Internal latent delta is not prediction error; delayed feature residual and percentile thresholds are proxies, and the active code updates a broader global encoder than a world-model-only reading suggests.
sc2wm.evidence: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 3 p.8 full SR 50.90 versus fixed-interval 50.30; supplement Table 6 no adaptation 49.86, entropy 49.48, asynchronous 50.19, FRL 50.90. INSPECTED CODE: TTA_setup_trainable_params:1030–1035 and ss_trainer_ETP.py:2246–2308.
sc2wm.followups: WorldMAP and PiJEPA are current primary-source leads reserved for follow-up audit; no reviewed matched residual-to-action-risk validation resolves this concern.

sgm.description: Predicted semantic targets can attract exploration toward confidently wrong room/object context.
sgm.conditions: Unusual layouts, segmentation errors or category combinations outside training.
sgm.cause: Map completion and argmax target selection use scores without demonstrated probability calibration; observed-map override protects observed cells but not unknown predictions.
sgm.evidence: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 2 p.7 full Gibson SR/SPL 78.0/44.0 versus oracle target 91.7/72.3. DEDUCTION: oracle gap does not uniquely identify calibration as the cause.
sgm.followups: WMNav uses VLM curiosity and L2M ensembles uncertainty; neither establishes reliable recovery after confidently wrong semantic-map completion.

sgm.description: The inspected hard IoU term cannot train the decoder through its detached thresholded mask.
sgm.conditions: The released main masked-map pretraining loss.
sgm.cause: Thresholding and detach remove the differentiable path for IoU, although weighted MSE and BCE still supply gradients.
sgm.evidence: INSPECTED CODE: main pretrainer imports models_mae_cross (lines 38,172); models_mae_cross.py:254–295 computes detached hard IoU. No training run was executed.
sgm.followups: No inspected patch or follow-up establishes the empirical effect of replacing the detached term with a differentiable surrogate.
sgm.status: Still unresolved in the reviewed literature
sgm.confidence: High for gradient path; unknown for benchmark impact

unemo.description: One provisional predicted state can bias all final action candidates.
unemo.conditions: The provisional action is wrong or several action-conditioned futures are plausible.
unemo.cause: A shared predicted future is fused back into action reasoning instead of maintaining separately validated counterfactual branches.
unemo.evidence: DEDUCTION: multimodal world-model/action pipeline; Tables 3–4 p.7 give best final-action-only 72.9 versus joint two-action 72.1, complicating a simple auxiliary-action-benefit claim.
unemo.followups: SC²-WM uses feature refinement and observed residual adaptation in CE; this is not a matched resolution of UNeMo candidate conditioning.

unemo.description: Missing world-model objective/attention details and unavailable verified training source prevent faithful reproduction.
unemo.conditions: Implementing the printed CVAE and single-key attention description or reconciling headline versus best ablation.
unemo.cause: The supplied specification does not establish all training losses and tensor semantics; no complete official repository was verified.
unemo.evidence: UNVERIFIED: method equations and Tables 1,3–4, PDF pp.4–7; headline SR 72.1 versus final-action-only 72.9 is not a single interchangeable configuration.
unemo.followups: No inspected supplementary implementation or follow-up resolves these details.

vid2world.description: Temporal causal masking and guidance do not establish intervention-valid or calibrated transition probabilities.
vid2world.conditions: Unsupported actions, abrupt dynamics changes or physical policy deployment.
vid2world.cause: Chronological conditioning prevents future leakage but does not remove confounding in logged action data; guidance changes conditional distributions and linear extrapolation assumes local regularity.
vid2world.evidence: DEDUCTION: transfer/masking/guidance mechanism. PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 1 p.8 RECON FVD/LPIPS 59.4/.3236 versus NWM 31.2/.295, and the real-to-sim study ranks only three drawer-policy checkpoints.
vid2world.followups: NWM/LCVN/WorldVLN use video prediction differently; no reviewed cross-task intervention study establishes broad causal validity.

visualimaginations.description: Generated landmark prototypes may improve representation learning without faithfully predicting the current hidden scene.
visualimaginations.conditions: Unusual object appearances or claims that foresight causes the navigation gain.
visualimaginations.cause: Images are semantic prototypes derived from instruction phrases, not action-conditioned scene transitions; training losses remain beneficial when prototypes are removed at test time.
visualimaginations.evidence: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 3 p.6 correct/none/wrong imagination SR 67.26/66.92/66.24 versus baseline 66.24; selected attention maps do not establish causality.
visualimaginations.followups: MonoDream/FantasyVLN also exploit auxiliary prediction. Separate prototype alignment from actual-state prediction in any comparison; no causal deployment mediation test was reviewed.

visualplanning.description: Exact grid-state validators do not transfer automatically to noisy embodied outcomes.
visualplanning.conditions: Replacing synthetic grids with real visual navigation or manipulation.
visualplanning.cause: RL rewards and exact-match/progress scoring use a rule-based interpreter and known transition/task structure; a learned real-world validator can be wrong or exploitable.
visualplanning.evidence: AUTHOR METHOD and DEDUCTION: interpreter/reward formulation; Table 1 p.6 EM/PR 80.6/84.9 establishes gains within the synthetic domain only.
visualplanning.followups: CoT-VLA/FantasyVLN/WorldVLN use richer tasks without inheriting the exact validator. No reviewed real-world counterpart preserves the same correctness guarantees.

vlnsig.description: Auxiliary future-token prediction has not been shown to improve actions specifically by forecasting correct future content.
vlnsig.conditions: Distinguishing representation regularization from deployed foresight.
vlnsig.cause: Future-token and semantic objectives train the encoder; dVAE/CLIP targets and vocabulary select what information is retained, while prediction heads are not an explicit deployment simulator.
vlnsig.evidence: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 2 p.6 baseline SR/SPL 64.4/58.8 versus all 68.1/62.3; supplement p.3 visual reconstructions use 70% ground-truth tokens, so they are not autonomous predicted images.
vlnsig.followups: MonoDream/FantasyVLN share training-time prediction; NavQ inserts predicted semantics during inference. No matched intervention demonstrates causal future-content use in VLN-SIG.

wmnav.description: An ordinary cell that receives a falsely low curiosity score cannot recover merely because a later score rises.
wmnav.cause: The ordinary update takes the minimum of old and new values, creating irreversible pessimism; identified goal-mask cells are an explicit exception reset to 10.
wmnav.evidence: INSPECTED CODE: _merge_evalue and update_curiosity_value:1263–1287. EXECUTED TEST: isolated 10→2→9 merge gives 10→2→2; goal reset produces 10. Not a simulator performance test.
wmnav.followups: Goal-mask reset resolves recovery for those identified cells only. SGM/L2M use different maps, with no matched ordinary-cell recovery intervention reviewed.
wmnav.confidence: High for update behavior; unknown for aggregate success impact

wmnav.description: Heuristic VLM curiosity scores and stopping choices vary substantially with backbone and configuration.
wmnav.conditions: Transferring the recipe to smaller VLMs or comparing different HM3D versions.
wmnav.cause: Prompt responses are not calibrated probabilities; paper and source stopping thresholds differ and models differ in semantic judgment.
wmnav.evidence: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table III p.6 Qwen3B SR 29.7 versus Gemini1.5Pro 58.1; INSPECTED CODE uses 0.8m internally, while printed 1.0/0.1m threshold is inconsistent. Evaluation success threshold is a separate setting.
wmnav.followups: ImagineNav++ adds memory and SGM/L2M change score sources; none establishes backbone-invariant calibration under a matched protocol.

womap.description: Optimizing detector-derived reward can favor visible/confident objects without ensuring physically valid goal reaching.
womap.conditions: Background/lighting shift or candidate actions outside the learned dynamics support.
womap.cause: Gradient search amplifies errors in learned dynamics and rewards; evaluation success also uses detector confidence/box-size thresholds, potentially sharing reward bias.
womap.evidence: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 2 p.8 nominal success 63% falls to 50% lighting and 30% background shift. INSPECTED CODE: optional reward/std score exists; joint planner differs from printed smoothing objective.
womap.followups: DINO-WM/NWM offer other models and CVAML addresses value-objective bias. None is a matched resolution of detector-based goal/reward validity.
womap.status: Still unresolved in the reviewed literature

worldmodels.description: A controller can achieve high imagined reward by exploiting a poorly supported world model.
worldmodels.conditions: Low-temperature learned Doom dynamics and policy-induced distribution shift.
worldmodels.cause: Random-policy training undercovers controller-induced states, and the controller searches weaknesses of the learned transition/reward process.
worldmodels.evidence: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 2 p.4 temperature .1 gives virtual/real survival 2086/193; at 1.15, 918/1092. Section 4.2 p.6 explicitly discusses exploitation.
worldmodels.followups: PlaNet/Dreamer collect policy experience iteratively and use stronger latent training. This mitigates mismatch but does not prove robustness of unsupported imagined trajectories.

worldvln.description: Segmented imagined execution can delay correction until a new real observation arrives.
worldvln.conditions: Aerial navigation with environment changes or prediction errors inside an action segment.
worldvln.cause: Real-history assimilation is intermittent; within-segment decisions can depend on predicted video rather than fresh measurements.
worldvln.evidence: AUTHOR METHOD and DEDUCTION: segmented rollout/observation assimilation; Table 1 aerial UAVFlow results do not isolate feedback-delay sensitivity.
worldvln.followups: CoT-VLA has a related chunk-feedback issue; LCVN/NWM use different offline protocols. No matched delay-versus-risk intervention was reviewed.

worldvln.description: A time-dependent common positive reward scale can cancel under per-group standardized advantages.
worldvln.conditions: Advantages normalized separately for a group sharing the same positive temporal scale, apart from epsilon effects.
worldvln.cause: Both mean-subtracted rewards and their standard deviation scale by the same factor; this does not hold automatically if groups mix times or the implementation normalizes differently.
worldvln.evidence: DEDUCTION/EXECUTED TEST: evidence/02/logic_check_results.json verifies the algebra numerically for a toy reward vector. The official snapshot is a project site, and the unreleased trainer grouping remains unknown.
worldvln.followups: No inspected official trainer or correction determines whether the printed temporal factor has the intended effect in the actual training run.
worldvln.confidence: High for conditional algebra; unknown for actual trainer behavior
